answer.summary: Severity: High. In src/files.py, read_public() concatenates the user-supplied string directly onto the root Path ((root / user_path).read_text(...)) without calling .resolve() or verifying the result remains under root. README.md states the intended boundary is 'serve files below one public root.' Exploit condition: a caller passes user_path containing '..' segments (e.g. '../../etc/passwd') or an absolute path; pathlib's '/' operator does not normalize or confine, so the resolved target escapes the public root and reads an arbitrary file. No containment check exists in the implementation.
